neighbours.label: verse: words inside lines of rhymed, metered poetry laid out line by line (often archaic or hymn style); the same imagery written as ordinary prose stays low
fire:
The old hymn runs:
O lead us through the darkened vale,
Where weary pilgrims fall and fail,
And guide us home when night is long.

From an old ballad:
The miller's daughter, fair and young,
Went down the lane with song unsung,
And waited by the willow tree.

A verse from the album:
When autumn leaves begin to fall,
And shadows climb the garden wall,
I think of you and all we said.

The epitaph reads:
Here lies a man of honest heart,
Who played on earth a humble part,
And asked no more than daily bread.

He recited:
The ships came sailing up the bay,
At break of dawn on Christmas day,
With banners bright and voices loud.

The poem closes:
So let the world go spinning on,
The hours we had are quickly gone,
But love remains when all is done.

A schoolbook rhyme:
Upon the hill the shepherd stands,
His crook held firmly in his hands,
And watches as the lambs go by.

The second stanza:
Thy mercy, Lord, is like the sea,
As wide and deep and full and free,
It reaches every distant shore.
quiet: The old guidebook says that pilgrims crossing the dark valley often grew tired and lost their way at night.
In the old story, the miller's young daughter walked down the lane and waited quietly by the willow tree.
On the album notes, the singer explains that autumn always reminds her of an old friend.
The gravestone records that he was an honest man who lived a humble life and asked for little.
He described how the ships sailed into the bay at dawn on Christmas day with their flags flying.
The essay closes by saying that time passes quickly, but love remains after everything else.
In the schoolbook picture, a shepherd stands on the hill holding his crook and watching the lambs.
The sermon compared God's mercy to the sea, wide and deep enough to reach every shore.

notes: Card: all top examples are poems or hymns with line breaks (Shakespeare-like, 'Lead on O King Eternal', 'Together round her grave we played'). Probe: four-line rhymed poem 0.954, 'And when the winds of winter blew, / We gathered round' 0.648, sonnet couplet 0.209, song lyrics 0.080; the same imagery as prose 0.031, 'sceptre ... temporal power' in prose 0.008, report 0.004.
